statement.p: A biologist has been observing a trees height. This type of tree typically grows by 0.23 feet each month. Fifteen months into the observation, the tree was 22.25 feet tall.

Let x be the number of months passed since the observations started, and let y be the trees height at that time, in feet. Use a linear equation to model the trees height as the number of months pass.
This lines slope-intercept equation is .
29 months after the observations started, the tree would be feet in height.
months after the observation started, the tree would be 32.37 feet tall.

li.p: A lines equation in slope-intercept form looks like y=mx+b, where m is the slope, and y is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept. Since the tree grows at a rate of 0.23 feet per month, 0.23 is the slope of the linear model.
So now we have that y=0.23x+b. The next step is to find the value of b. There are at least two ways.
One way is to substitute a known point into y=0.23x+b. We use the point (15,22.25).

p.m: \begin{aligned} y \amp = 0.23x + b \\ 22.25 \amp = 0.23 \cdot 15 + b \\ 22.25 \amp = 3.45 + b \\ 22.25\mathbf{{}-3.45} \amp = 3.45 + b\mathbf{{}-3.45} \\ 18.8 \amp = b\\ b \amp = 18.8 \end{aligned}

li.p: This lines slope-intercept equation is y=0.23x+18.8.
Another way is to use the lines point-slope equation y-y_{1}=m(x-x_{1}). Again, we use the point (15,22.25).
This is the second way to find b, and thus the lines slope-intercept equation is y=0.23x+18.8.
